paraphrase: Gārgī asks Yājñavalkya for the yoga that leads to liberation, and he teaches the eight-limbed yoga: yama, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna and samādhi.

paraphrase: The ten restraints are non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence, compassion, straightforwardness, forbearance, fortitude, moderate diet and purity; the ten observances (in the next chapter) include austerity, contentment, faith, giving, worship of the Lord, listening to doctrine, modesty, intelligence, repetition and vows.

paraphrase: One form of withdrawal is to draw the breath from one vital point (marma) to the next along the eighteen vital points of the body, holding it at each; this is taught among five kinds of withdrawal.
